transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi Doctor. I'm a 37-year-old firefighter, and when I’m not on an actual call, I just can’t keep my attention on training, reports, or manuals long enough to get through them properly. It's become a really big obstacle lately because I'm trying to do the coursework and paperwork to promote to captain.
Did you also have similar problems with attention, organization, or restlessness when you were a child or teenager, before age 12?

Yes, absolutely, it goes all the way back to elementary school. My teachers were constantly moving my seat because I wouldn't stop talking, and I'd always forget to turn in homework I had actually finished. Every report card back then said I was smart but just couldn't sit still or stay focused in class.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [F90.0, F98.8], but the new history strongly supports a persistent childhood-onset pattern of inattention and hyperactivity starting before age 12, with clear impairment in school and now at work. That makes F98.8 unlikely because the symptoms are not better explained by a residual/other specified behavioral presentation; the presentation is most consistent with a neurodevelopmental attention/hyperactivity disorder. The current candidate is therefore F90.0.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a longstanding pattern since childhood of inattention and hyperactive/impulsive behavior, with current impairment in work-related training, reports, and paperwork. Symptoms began before age 12 and have persisted into adulthood, consistent with ADHD, predominantly inattentive presentation / attention deficit disorder without hyperactivity coding in ICD-10.
